correctness.rationale: The tree-edge polynomial is F_m=sum_i a_i b_i product_(j!=i)(a_j+b_j). Gauss induction uses gcd(F_(s-1),product u_j)=1. Partition singular points by zero count of u_i: zero zeroes has nonzero derivative of sum v_i/u_i; one zero forces a_i=b_i=0 and remaining F_(m-1)=0; two zeroes force two zero coordinate pairs; at least three u_i=0 gives L_I. All components are irreducible, same dimension and distinct on explicit dense opens. Nondegenerate Hessians of local equations st U+(s+t)w and sum_(pairs) v_i u_j u_k give generic 3-variable nodes. Hypersurface is S2 and R1, hence normal. Independent full projective GF(5) m=3, GF(3) m=4 and GF(2) m=5 enumeration reproduced Jacobian/component incidence exactly on respectively 3906, 3280 and 1023 projective points, with singular counts 121, 652, 671; m=3 used only as boundary corroboration. This is not an all-m proof; the symbolic argument is.

value.rationale: An explicit irreducible-component/degree and transverse-singularity classification of a natural infinite family of graph-configuration hypersurfaces extends the known prism example and supplies concrete local models beyond general determinantal support. m=4 has eight components of total degree twenty; the arithmetic of components is not a routine direct corollary of the general rank criterion.

final_claim: For char-0 algebraically closed k and each m>=4, the K_(2,m) spanning-tree hypersurface has reduced singular components C_i (m irreducible degree-m sections) and L_I (binomial(m,3) linear spaces), all dimension 2m-4, degree m^2+binomial(m,3), with generic transverse 3-variable nondegenerate quadratic double points; the integral hypersurface is normal.
limitations: No nonreduced Jacobian structure or nongeneric crossing models.
